about.title: Los Altos Hills Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Los Altos Hills is a small, quiet community, but its winding roads and busy connectors like I-280 and Page Mill Road still see their share of serious crashes. Recent public records show 34 injury collisions and 51 people hurt in a single year, with a concentration of reported crashes on Tuesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. — a window when commuter traffic mixes with local drivers navigating hills and curves. Whether your crash happened on the freeway, along Purissima Road, or at a smaller intersection, the aftermath can bring medical bills, lost work, and confusing calls from insurance adjusters. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that helps injured people in Los Altos Hills get matched with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, explain your options under California law, and handle communications with insurers on your behalf while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a county road agency, may be involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Recover
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you were partly at fault, but your share of fault can lower the final amount. Having someone review the crash details and any local road reports can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed and no fee unless there's a recovery. This lets you get legal guidance without adding financial pressure while you're already dealing with medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to look for inconsistencies or minimize what they later offer. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on I-280 or Page Mill Road and I'm not sure who's at fault?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so you can still pursue a claim even if fault is shared or unclear. Corridors like I-280 and Page Mill Road see a mix of freeway speeds and local turns, which can complicate fault determinations. An attorney can help gather evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness accounts, to clarify what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to take action after a Los Altos Hills car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That timeframe can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, if a government entity's road or vehicle was involved. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to have your case reviewed sooner rather than later.
